notes: Seven mechanical greps (C1-C7, one per category from the task brief plus C7 added mid-review for a PL/pgSQL trigger instance the original six categories' commands could not reach) run from the repo root against the working tree at time of read. Per-command scoping notes are attached to each key below. All commands exclude *.test.ts; the task's own scope note says tests/harness only count if a shadow list there gates production behaviour, and no test-level shadow list meeting that bar was found -- the one credible candidate (harness's synthetic AccountingProvider being behind the real interface) is reported in findings.md as a corroborating observation, not enumerated here, because it is an interface-completeness gap rather than a union-membership shadow and because the review did not independently reproduce the sibling process's exact measurement (see findings.md). IMPORTANT: this branch had four other agents actively editing src/ concurrently for the full duration of this review (confirmed via repeated `git status` checks and line numbers shifting between reads of the same file). Line numbers below are as read at the time of read, stated per-item in coverage.json where a site was re-read after drift was noticed. `git status --short` immediately before this file was written showed active modifications to: src/control-kernel/accountingCaseCompiler.ts, src/domain/accountingCase.ts, src/domain/accountingCasePersistence.ts, src/policy/xeroNativeRouteContract.ts, src/services/xeroAccountingCaseService.ts (plus several harness/scripts/tests files outside this review's src/ scope). No migrations/*.sql file was among the files being concurrently modified, which is itself relevant to SR-14.

C1_ternary_fallback_candidate.scoping_note: Proxy for a ternary chain's continuation lines (a line that is itself only `: cond ? a : b`, i.e. the tail of a nested ternary begun on a prior line). Not exhaustive for every ternary chain shape in the repo -- it catches multi-line chained ternaries specifically, which is the shape of the task's confirmed instance. Single-line ternary chains (like the confirmed instance itself, xeroBusinessCoordinateAuthority.ts:34-40, which IS multi-line) and ternaries embedded inside a single expression without their own line were located by manual union cross-referencing instead, documented as such in coverage.json.

C2_switch_over_union.scoping_note: Every `switch (` statement in src/ (test files excluded). Each was read in full to determine whether it switches over a closed union, whether it is exhaustive today, and whether it would be compiler-caught if the union grew.

C3_zod_enum_literal_array.scoping_note: z.enum([...]) calls with a literal array argument -- the risky hand-typed form. Deliberately excludes z.enum(SOME_CONST_ARRAY) (no bracket immediately after the paren), which is the safe array-derived form (e.g. z.enum(XERO_SINGAPORE_ACCOUNTING_CATEGORY_KEYS) in xeroTenantCoaProfile.ts) and was not counted as a candidate for this reason, noted explicitly here rather than silently dropped.

C4_record_type.scoping_note: Every Record<...> reference in src/ except Record<string, ...> (a generic string index is not a union-membership shadow candidate). Each site was classified by whether it is a plain type annotation (protected -- see probe4.ts), a `satisfies` annotation (protected, the task brief's reference pattern), or an `as` cast (unprotected -- see probe5.ts), and whether the cast is nonetheless safe by construction because its key set is array-derived.

C5_as_const_array_or_inline_iteration.command: grep -rn "for (const .* of \[" src --include="*.ts" | grep -v "\.test\.ts" | sort; grep -rn "\] as const)" src --include="*.ts" | grep -v "\.test\.ts" | sort
C5_as_const_array_or_inline_iteration.scoping_note: Inline array literals iterated with for-of, plus `] as const)` closings (inline as-const arrays used as an argument, e.g. `(X as const).some(...)`). Both are candidate closed-membership lists that might restate a union instead of deriving one. Field-validation loops that merely iterate a fixed set of INPUT FIELDS (not union members) were read and marked not-applicable rather than excluded from the enumeration.

C6_sql_check_constraint.scoping_note: SQL CHECK constraints in migrations/*.sql whose column name suggests a closed domain enumeration (state/status/kind/type/route/action/class/disposition). jsonb_typeof shape guards and cross-column consistency checks that happened to match the keyword filter were read and marked not-applicable rather than excluded.

C7_sql_trigger_hardcoded_action_id_branc.scoping_note: Added after reading migrations/039's accounting_case_operation_guard() trigger function and finding it hand-enumerates action_id inside PL/pgSQL, a shadow of AccountingCaseOperation['actionId'] entirely outside anything tsc can see. This command finds every hardcoded action_id string-literal branch across all migrations so the full lineage (which copies are superseded vs live, and how many distinct trigger functions carry the pattern) could be traced rather than asserted from the one instance first noticed.

C1b_ternary_head_broadened.scoping_note: Added after discovering the original, narrower C1 command (`^\s*: .* ? .* : .*$`) does not match the task brief's own confirmed SR-01 instance (`const x = route === "A" ? ... : route === "B" ? ... : fallback` does not begin with a leading `:`). This broadened command finds the HEAD line of a ternary assignment comparing a dotted-path expression against an uppercase string literal -- catches both the confirmed instance and many more candidates, at the cost of also matching many genuinely-safe binary ternaries (each was read and classified individually in coverage.json; not all 32 hits could be traced to the same depth in the time remaining -- 17 were marked NOT_EXAMINED with the reason stated per-item).
